To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the number of trees is the most important hyperparameter for tuning random forest, (2) the number of variables to be considered at each split is the most important tuning hyperparameter of the algorithms that we examined and (3) for most algorithms, the default values for the hyperparameters are reasonable.

the question how the performance of machine learning algorithms is influenced by their hyperparameters.
the tuning of hyperparameters for random forest and machine learning algorithms in general.
the question of what hyperparameters should be chosen to optimize the performance of a machine learning algorithm.

the number of variables that is considered at each split is the most tunable hyperparameter, while the minimum number of samples per node is the least tunable.

random forest is very robust against changes of hyperparameters, which is also reflected by its popularity in practice.

random forest is very tunable and it is worth to tune it.
